label: COMMUNICATION

cover.headline: How to listen so *he keeps talking*
cover.sub: 5 small shifts that make it easier to open up.

points.heading: Put the phone out of reach
points.body: Not face down. Out of reach. It’s the clearest way to say this matters.
points.panel: Leave it in another room for ten minutes.

points.heading: Let the pause sit
points.body: Silence often means he’s still thinking. Count to five before you fill it.
points.panel: Wait one breath longer than feels natural.

points.heading: Reflect before you respond
points.body: Say back what you heard. It shows you were listening and catches misunderstandings early.
points.panel: “So it felt like nobody had your back. Is that right?”

points.heading: Hold the fix
points.body: Sometimes he wants a solution. Often he wants to be heard first. You can ask which.
points.panel: “Do you want ideas, or do you want me to just listen?”

points.heading: Thank him for telling you
points.body: Opening up is a risk. A little appreciation makes the next time easier.

close.save: Save this for your next real talk.

caption:
It’s easy to listen while quietly preparing a reply. He can tell. So can you, when it’s done to you.

Listening well is less about saying the right thing and more about making room. These five shifts are small, and you can try any one of them tonight.

Save this, and follow @spotseason for more small steps.
